messages:
mika: Heads up — found a public S3 object that contains what looks like a wrapped credential blob for analytics-prod. incident-bot created INC-2026 :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026 created by mika.
mika: Excerpt: `vault:transit:kms-us-west1/keys/ri-transit|wrapped:Cg...` Bucket: s3://redwood-logs-archive/2026-03-12/events.log — unsure if it's Vault-wrapped ciphertext or raw SA key.
jess: @mika thanks. we should assume compromise until proven otherwise. priority: rotation + audit + short-term RBAC lockdown. Who can list KMS key versions?
lee: Logs show calls to `vault/transit/decrypt` that proxied to KMS key ring `prod/ri-transit` around the same timestamp. So Vault transit leverages KMS — both could be impacted.
samir: Proposed immediate actions: 1) disable the GCP service account bound to analytics-prod, 2) revoke any Vault tokens associated, 3) create a new KMS key version and rewrap secrets, 4) issue new credentials and update deployments, 5) ship audit exports to compliance. Maintenance window suggestion: 23:00 UTC tonight.
mika: I'm locking down blast radius now: disabling SA and cordoning jobs. Running:
```
# disable SA
gcloud iam service-accounts disable analytics-prod-sa@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# revoke known Vault accessors (replace <ACCESSOR>)
vault auth token revoke -accessor <ACCESSOR>
```
jess: For Vault: do NOT delete secrets. Instead rotate and preserve history. Plan: write new secret and version it. Example:
```
# write new creds to kv v2
vault kv put secret/analytics/prod @new-creds.json
# record audit device snapshot
cp /var/log/vault_audit.log /exports/compliance/INC-2026/vault_audit_snapshot.log
```
lee: RBAC mitigation: create temporary deny policy for analytics roles and bind to the relevant principals. I'll open a short-lived policy `deny-analytics-sa` and add to infra roles. PR incoming, tagging infra-oncall.
mika: Searching for other exposures now: `rg -n "analytics-prod-sa" /mnt/logs || true` and checking S3 access logs for anonymous or unusual activity. If you have quick grep queries, ping me.
samir: Also check KMS key versions and last usage: `gcloud kms keys versions list --key=ri-transit --location=us-west1 --keyring=prod --format=json | jq .` If we see recent decrypt calls from unknown IPs, bump key version and rewrap. Consider creating a new key and scheduling deprecation of the old.
jess: Rotation runbook (proposed timeline):
- 23:00 UTC: disable SA, revoke short-lived tokens, cordon analytics pods
- 23:05 UTC: create new KMS key version / or new key if warranted
- 23:10 UTC: rewrap Vault transit secrets to new key version (`vault write transit/rewrap ...`)
- 23:20 UTC: update deployments with new credentials + run smoke tests
- 23:50 UTC: if smoke OK, update IAM roles and re-enable SA with new credentials
- 00:00 UTC: publish audit export and close INC-2026 (or escalate)
Please ack on availability.
mika: ack. I'll pull audit logs and run initial forensics, snapshot the S3 object and its headers, and upload to /exports/compliance/INC-2026. tagging @security-bot for automated export.
security-bot: export scheduled: /exports/compliance/INC-2026/ — files: vault_audit_snapshot.log, kms_activity.json, s3_object_dump.txt
lee: I'll send RBAC PR now. Small ask: Platform, can you stand by to run rollback playbook if smoke tests fail?
oncall-bot: @eng-oncall requested. Playbook available: rollback to previous secret version in Vault KV and revert KMS key version. ETA 30m to get an oncall.
eng-oncall: Oncall available. Confirmed rollback steps and will monitor during rotation.
jess: One more compliance note — record an entry in the vault audit with the reason for rotation and link to INC-2026. Also add a note in the security-runbook about verifying no other wrapped blobs in the log bucket.
mika: Will do. I'll create a follow-up ticket to audit all archived log objects for similar patterns and add a long-term action to require server-side KMS encryption on log uploads.
samir: After rotation, schedule a rekey for Vault transit (create new transit key and rewrap), and run a policy audit to ensure no orphaned accessors remain.
jess: Thanks team. I'll coordinate the rotation and post completion summary here. :white_check_mark:
